title: Eternal Source of Light and Thought
description: Eternal Source of Light and Thought in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 74 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Subjection to the Father of Spirits”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-ter-nal Source of light and thought! Be all be-neath thy-self for-got, Whilst thee, great par-ent mind, we own, In pros-trate hom-age round thy throne.

lines: Eternal Source of light and thought!
Whilst thee, great parent-mind, we own,
In prostrate homage round thy throne.
Whilst in themselves our souls survey
Of thee some faint reflected ray,
They wondering to their Father rise:
His power how vast! his thoughts how wise!
O may we live before thy face,
The willing subjects of thy grace;
And through each path of duty move,
With filial awe, and filial love.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
